library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(naniar)
library(ggmap)
library(lubridate)
library(shiny)
register_stadiamaps("06cd37b9-1de9-4a29-a487-f35c527a975f", write = FALSE)
polar_bears <- 
  read_csv("data/polarBear_serumUreaCreatinine_beaufortChukchi_rode.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(-den_method, -no_cubs, -cub_age) %>%
  filter(age_class==c("A", "S")) %>% 
  mutate(sex=toupper(sex), 
         age_class=toupper(age_class))
  1. (6 points) Is sampling even for both sexes? Make a count the shows the number of males and females sampled by population and make a plot to visualize the counts.
polar_bears %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=popn, fill = sex))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(title = "Sampling of Male vs Female Polar Bear Population", x="Population", y="Count", fill = "Sex")

No, the sampling isn’t even, there are more female bears sampled in the data.

  1. (6 points) How many bears were sampled in each year for both populations? Make a line plot(s) to visualize sampling by year for both populations. (hint: you will need to pull apart the date to get the year in its own column)
polar_bears_year <- polar_bears %>% 
  separate(capture_date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-") %>% 
  group_by(popn, year) %>% 
  summarize(count = n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=year, y=count, color=popn))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point(shape = 16)+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Sampling of Polar Bears by Year", x="Year", y="Count", color = "Population")
## `summarise()` has regrouped the output.
## ℹ Summaries were computed grouped by popn and year.
## ℹ Output is grouped by popn.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.groups = "drop_last")` to silence this message.
## ℹ Use `summarise(.by = c(popn, year))` for per-operation grouping
##   (`?dplyr::dplyr_by`) instead.
polar_bears_year
## `geom_line()`: Each group consists of only one observation.
## ℹ Do you need to adjust the group aesthetic?

polar_bears <- polar_bears %>%
  mutate(un_creat_ratio = (urea_nitrogen * 0.466) / creatinine)

  1. (6 points) The authors found that the number of fasting bears increased in the SB population but decreased in the CS population. Make a plot(s) that shows the number of fasting bears by year for both populations to visualize this trend.
polar_bears %>% 
  separate(capture_date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-") %>%
  filter(fasting == "fasting") %>%
  group_by(popn, year) %>% 
  summarize(count = n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=year, y=count, color=popn))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point(shape = 16) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Number of Fasting Bears by Year and Population", x="Year", y="Number of Fasting Bears", color = "Population")

  1. (8 points) Where are the polar bears used in this study located? Make a static (not leaflet) distribution map that shows the locations of bears by population. (hint: use color=popn in the aes() of geom_point())
polar_bears %>% 
  select(lat, long) %>% 
  summary()
##       lat             long       
##  Min.   :62.46   Min.   :-172.2  
##  1st Qu.:68.11   1st Qu.:-165.2  
##  Median :70.53   Median :-150.7  
##  Mean   :69.86   Mean   :-153.7  
##  3rd Qu.:71.00   3rd Qu.:-146.5  
##  Max.   :72.70   Max.   :-134.8
lat <- c(62.46, 72.7)
long <- c(-172.2, -134.8)
bbox <- make_bbox(long, lat, f=0.03)
map1 <- get_stadiamap(bbox, maptype="stamen_terrain", zoom=6)
## ℹ © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.
## ℹ 48 tiles needed, this may take a while (try a smaller zoom?)
ggmap(map1)+
  geom_point(data=polar_bears, aes(x=long, y=lat, color=popn), size=0.75, alpha=0.8)+
  labs(x="Longitude", y="Latitude", title="Locations of Polar Bears")

  1. (10 points) Build a simple shiny app that shows the range of un_creat_ratio values for both populations. The user should be able to select the fill variable and choose between sex, mating, age_class, denning, and fasting. Please use the code chunk below so that your exam knits.
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  
    selectInput("x", 
                "Select Variable",
                choices = c("sex", 
                            "mating",
                            "age_class",
                            "denning",
                            "fasting"),
                selected = "sex"),
  
    plotOutput("plot", width="500px", height="400px")
  )

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
output$plot <- renderPlot({
    
      polar_bears %>% 
      ggplot(aes(x = .data[[input$x]], 
               y = un_creat_ratio, 
               fill = .data[[input$x]])) +
      geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Range of UN:Creatinine Ratio by", tools::toTitleCase(input$x)),
        x = tools::toTitleCase(input$x),
        y = "UN:Creatinine Ratio",
        fill = tools::toTitleCase(input$x)
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
      theme(legend.position = "none")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
